title: Overseas Highway pavement markings
summary: Two straight-ahead arrows, nine divider dashes and 118 m of white edge stripe follow repeated public aerial observations southbound on US 1. The comparison retains the published photographic camera position and the same Godot camera in both renders.
measurement: The FDOT 2018 aerial independently supported 96.9% and 100% of the two recovered arrow footprints within 0.29 m. At the original uncalibrated photo pose, their mean centroid error was 32.6 pixels in an 820-pixel-wide image. Separately, an outer-frame optical fit and a 3.32 m observed travel lane predicted 9.8 pixels when the camera was centered in that lane. The Boston candidate failed its historical aerial check.

images.caption: The 2017 photograph and the two fixed-camera Metal renders show the same approach. The camera GPS lies near the surveyed right stripe, which changes its apparent position in the fixed render.
Normal Miata cockpit on the same 43.1 m southwest physics drive. The screenshots were taken after 16 m. All four tires stayed in contact throughout both runs.

Diagnostic camera pose from the outer frames and surveyed lane center. The actual Metal arrow centroids averaged 11.0 px from the unused photograph at 820 px wide. The published fixed-pose and normal player comparisons appear above.
